Duration::ge¶

Back to Duration API Reference

Signature¶

Series Duration::ge(const Duration& other) const;
Series Duration::operator>=(const Duration& other) const;  // ge(other)

What It Does¶

Compares two Duration values elementwise, testing whether self is greater than or equal to other by underlying elapsed-nanosecond magnitude, broadcasting under ordinary N-D rules, and returns a Series of booleans.

Parameters¶

other (const Duration&)

The duration to compare against. Broadcasts against self.

Returns¶

Series A boolean Series at the broadcasted shape, one comparison result per position.

Examples¶

Example 1. 1 day is greater than or equal to 1 hour.

auto one_hour = pluss::duration::hours(1);
auto one_day = pluss::duration::days(1);
std::cout << pluss::series::print(one_day.ge(one_hour));

Output¶

Series(shape=[], strides=[], dtype=bool, platform=cpu, numel=1, contiguous=true)
data=true

1 day >= 1 hour is true.

Notes¶

  • ge(other) is gt(other) || eq(other) — true whenever either the strict-greater-than or the equality comparison is true.

  • operator>= is documented sugar for ge — nothing is computed differently between the two spellings.

See Also¶

  • gt: the strict counterpart.

  • le: the opposite-direction non-strict comparison.

  • eq, ne: equality comparisons.
